topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and the biological basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can give rise to cancer depending on cellular susceptibility and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence that environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than its being solely a matter of inherited susceptibility or bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, with their effects often determined by metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotion of tumour growth and explain why a mutagen alone may not produce cancer.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue's biological context and conclude the discussion of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenicity and linking exposures to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence is gathered and interpreted to determine whether an exposure can cause cancer.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing consolidates the lecture's conclusions around the everyday balancing of cancer risks against benefits.
